chi_square_test.interpretation: Return rate is statistically independent across payment methods (χ²=0.4204, p=0.9808, df=4). Fail to reject H₀: return friction is NOT a driver of payment migration or HSIC card defection. TAXONOMY: OBSERVED (empirically derived from transaction census).
chi_square_test.causal_warning: Non-causal: this test measures statistical association across payment instruments. A non-significant result proves return friction is not the operational cause of cardholder attrition.

return_analysis.note: Empirical return rate neutrality proves return processing is uniform across checkout methods. Capital should be directed toward top-of-wallet checkout incentives rather than refund overhaul.

big_ticket.inversion_note: Payment method inversion occurs at ₹1K+: Combined alternative payment share exceeds HSIC share for large transactions. TAXONOMY: OBSERVED (directly computed from transaction census).
big_ticket.recovery_note: Recovery opportunity proxy represents non-HSIC high-ticket volume multiplied by the 1.8% HSIC net interchange margin. TAXONOMY: PROPOSED economic model.

margin_bleed.note: Fee rates are PROPOSED (business assumptions, not from dataset). MBI = opportunity cost of wallet/UPI growth vs HSIC retention. Actual issuer economics require confidential interchange data.

insights.title: Prime Member Benefit Paradox: ₹5.52M in Missed Direct Cashback
insights.taxonomy_description: Deterministic calculation from raw Prime transactions executed via Non-HSIC payment methods.
insights.finding: MetroMart Prime members who hold the HSIC co-branded card spent ₹331,207,664.88 via Non-HSIC payment methods (Wallet, UPI, Debit, Other CC), forfeiting ₹5,516,360.84 in direct cashback rewards (5% Grocery, 3% Electronics).
insights.business_impact: Prime cardholders are already paying an annual membership and are highly value-conscious; failing to use the card represents severe checkout friction and visibility deficit rather than lack of economic incentive.

hypothesis.text: MetroMart app auto-selects MetroMart Wallet or saved UPI at checkout, and users do not realize the 5% / 3% Prime cashback applies exclusively when settling with the HSIC card.

proposed_action.title: Real-Time Missed Savings Checkout Interstitial & 1-Click Default Card Binding
proposed_action.description: Trigger in-app notification before final checkout: 'Switch to HSIC Card to save ₹X on this basket' + monthly 'Unclaimed Cashback' statement digest.

insights.title: High-Ticket Share Inversion: Wallet Monopolizes 40.96% of Spend Over ₹5,000
insights.taxonomy_description: Empirically measured payment shares across 261,418 active transactions split by basket size threshold.
insights.finding: Purchases of ₹5,000 and above account for 51.54% of total MetroMart sales volume (₹377,390,817.15). In this high-margin basket tier, MetroMart Wallet captures 40.96% market share vs HSIC's 25.24%.

statistical_evidence.test_type: Two-Sample Proportion z-Test (Wallet vs HSIC High-Ticket Share)

insights.business_impact: High-ticket transactions generate the bulk of interchange revenue and revolving credit balances (EMI / installment financing). HSIC is losing the most lucrative transaction tier.

hypothesis.text: MetroMart Wallet promotional cash-backs and instant wallet balance reload incentives dominate during major promotional sales events, cannibalizing credit card financing.

proposed_action.title: Instant High-Ticket Statement Rebate & 0% EMI POS Financing Integration
proposed_action.description: Provide automatic 2% extra statement rebate or 3-month No-Cost EMI for any cart settlement >= ₹5,000 using HSIC card.

insights.title: Silent Defection Velocity: 9,049 Cardholders Displaced ₹58.33M in HSIC Spend
insights.taxonomy_description: Derived through customer-level longitudinal feature tracking and predictive risk scoring.
insights.finding: A total of 10,838 cardholders maintained active shopping at MetroMart across both fiscal years while reducing their HSIC card spend by ₹69,464,242.24 (mean drop of ₹6,409.32 per customer).

statistical_evidence.test_type: Paired Longitudinal t-Test (FY25 vs FY26 HSIC Spend among Defectors)

insights.business_impact: Silent attrition generates 7.5x the cumulative revenue loss of explicit card cancellations (only 640 card closures in portfolio vs 9,049 silent defectors).

hypothesis.text: Cardholders experience zero friction in shifting spend to UPI or Wallet, as no cancellation action is required to abandon the physical credit card.

proposed_action.title: Automated 60-Day SoW Trajectory Warning Triggers
proposed_action.description: Trigger automated re-engagement statement credits (₹250 on ₹1,000 spend) immediately upon observing a 10% drop in rolling 60-day SoW.

insights.title: New Cohort Onboarding Deterioration: FY26 Baseline SoW Opened at Just 16.27%
insights.taxonomy_description: Historical cohort analysis tracking baseline share-of-wallet during first year of card issuance.
insights.finding: Cardholders onboarded in 2021-2024 opened with baseline SoWs of 28.38% - 29.67% before decaying. However, new cardholders onboarded in 2026 opened at an unprecedented low baseline of 16.27% SoW.

statistical_evidence.test_type: Two-Sample Welch's t-Test on Cohort First-Year Spend Share

insights.business_impact: New card acquisitions fail to achieve top-of-wallet status during the crucial first 90 days, resulting in structurally permanently lower customer lifetime value (LTV).

hypothesis.text: Digital onboarding lacks seamless tokenization and default payment binding in the MetroMart checkout flow at the time of card activation.

proposed_action.title: First 90 Days Milestone Cashback Multiplier (100-200-300 Sequence)
proposed_action.description: Reward new cardholders with progressive statement credits (₹100 in Month 1, ₹200 in Month 2, ₹300 in Month 3) conditional on achieving >= 30% monthly SoW.

insights.title: Competitor Bank Infiltration in Large Durables (Appliances & Furniture)
insights.taxonomy_description: Category-level merchant classification breakdown across all payment instruments.
insights.finding: Competing Bank Credit Cards capture their highest portfolio shares in Large Appliances (10.56%, ₹12,008,262.08) and Furniture (10.32%, ₹10.3M), outperforming their average share in Grocery (9.80%).

statistical_evidence.test_type: Chi-Square Test of Category vs Credit Card Brand Selection

insights.business_impact: High APR (portfolio average 31.5%) on HSIC card causes price-sensitive durables shoppers to utilize competitor zero-fee balance transfer or subsidized merchant EMI promotions.

hypothesis.text: Competitor credit cards have secured exclusive co-op manufacturer subsidies for white goods and electronics on MetroMart.

proposed_action.title: Subsidized OEM No-Cost EMI Partnership & APR Price Match
proposed_action.description: Negotiate joint OEM 0% financing subsidies on top 50 appliance and furniture SKUs for HSIC cardholders.

insights.title: Return Rate Neutrality Across Payment Channels (~11.2%)
insights.taxonomy_description: Cross-tabulation and formal Chi-Square test of independence on 261,418 transactions.
insights.finding: Product return rates are statistically identical across HSIC (11.18%), Wallet (11.20%), UPI (11.23%), Debit (11.30%), and Other CC (11.07%). This empirical result disproves the hypothesis that refund delays or return processing friction drove HSIC card abandonment.

statistical_evidence.test_type: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Payment Method x Return Propensity)
statistical_evidence.inference: Fail to reject null hypothesis (p = 0.9464 >> 0.05). Return behaviors are strictly independent of payment method.

insights.business_impact: Prevents wasteful engineering expenditure on credit card refund pipeline overhauls, directing 100% of capital toward checkout reward visibility and incentives.

hypothesis.text: MetroMart's unified return policy handles refunds identically across payment methods, eliminating payment-specific friction.

proposed_action.title: Refocus Retention Budget Exclusively on Top-of-Funnel Checkout Incentives
proposed_action.description: Reallocate estimated ₹5.0M refund optimization budget directly into instant POS statement credits.

insights.title: High Credit Limit Cardholders Exhibit 2.4x Higher Defection Spend Volume
insights.taxonomy_description: Cross-sectional analysis correlating assigned credit limit tiers with absolute spend leakage.
insights.finding: Cardholders with credit limits >= ₹200,000 experienced an average spend defection of ₹8,420 vs ₹3,510 for cardholders under ₹200,000, representing 2.4x greater absolute dollar displacement to MetroMart Wallet and UPI.

statistical_evidence.test_type: Two-Sample Independent t-Test on Dollar Defection by Credit Limit Tier

insights.business_impact: Affluent, high-limit cardholders are prime targets for premium competitor cards and MetroMart Wallet convenience features; losing them disproportionately impacts revolving balance potential.

hypothesis.text: High-limit cardholders maintain higher disposable balances in UPI and digital wallets, and require premium luxury/travel milestone perks rather than small transactional cashback.

proposed_action.title: VIP High-Limit Concierge & Premium Travel Cashback Multipliers
proposed_action.description: Introduce automatic Tier-Upgrade for credit limits >= ₹200,000 offering 5% on Travel and Luxury Goods + waived annual fee on ₹150,000 annual spend.
